title: /api/draft-capital returns 200 with real pick dollar values to an unauthenticated caller, and takes 13.2s doing it
claimUnderTest: Private valuation data is behind auth; only /api/public/* is anonymous.
observed: An anonymous GET returns HTTP 200 with a 15,989-byte board of per-pick dollar values in 13,188 ms. Every other value-bearing route (/api/data, /api/movers, /api/terminal, /api/valuation/league-adjusted) correctly 401s anonymously.

reproduction.expected: 401 unauthorized, consistent with every other value-bearing route

numericProof.formula: observed HTTP status and wall time

userImpact: Pick valuations that the rest of the platform treats as private are readable by anyone who can reach the API host, and the 13 s response makes the route a cheap way to consume backend capacity.

priorFinding.note: Measured directly in this audit's unauthenticated route sweep.

whatWorks: The rest of the auth boundary is consistent — 47 of 66 probed GET routes correctly 401 anonymously.
rootCause: The route is not wrapped by the auth dependency the other value routes use; the latency comes from a blocking Sleeper call for team-name mapping that fails and is retried inline (backend log: 'Sleeper API failed for draft capital team-name mapping').
requiredRepair: Apply the same auth gate as /api/data, and make the Sleeper team-name lookup non-blocking with a bounded timeout.

title: GET /api/bdvm/roster takes 48 seconds to return 310 bytes
claimUnderTest: BDVM endpoints self-suppress cheaply when no projection snapshot exists (CLAUDE.md: the /rankings gap column 'gates on status == ok so it self-suppresses').
observed: With data/bdvm/ absent, the endpoint still spends 47,994 ms before returning a 310-byte payload. Suppression is happening, but only after the full computation path has been walked.

reproduction.expected: a fast negative — the precondition (no snapshot) is knowable up front

numericProof.formula: wall time of a single authenticated GET

userImpact: The /bdvm page blocks for ~48 s before rendering an empty state. On a shared backend this also occupies a worker for the whole window.

priorFinding.note: Latency measured in this audit; the prior audit noted BDVM had never run in production but not this cost.

rootCause: To be confirmed by W13/W26 profiling — the snapshot-absent check appears to run after the roster/board assembly rather than before it.
requiredRepair: Check for the projection snapshot before doing any per-player work, and return the documented unpriced/no-snapshot payload immediately.
dependencies: W13 (BDVM) and W26 (performance) hold the call-path profile.

title: /api/data is 11.95 MB, not the ~4 MB CLAUDE.md documents, and view=compact is larger than view=app
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'view=full (default, backward-compat): returns the full canonical contract (~4 MB uncompressed)'.
observed: Measured 11,953,535 bytes uncompressed (1,176,182 gzipped) — about 3x the documented figure. Separately, ?view=compact returns 7,363,760 bytes while ?view=app returns 5,818,304, so the view named 'compact' is 27% LARGER than the app view.

reproduction.command: for v in '' '?view=app' '?view=compact'; do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -o /dev/null -w "$v %{size_download}\n" "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data$v"; done
reproduction.expected: ~4 MB full per the documentation; compact <= app

userImpact: A reader sizing work off CLAUDE.md underestimates the payload threefold, and anyone reaching for 'compact' to reduce bytes gets more of them.
whatWorks: GZipMiddleware is effective — 11.95 MB compresses to 1.18 MB on the wire.
rootCause: Documentation was written against an older contract; the compact view's field set has grown past the app view's.
requiredRepair: Correct the documented figures and either rename or re-scope view=compact so its name matches its size.

title: server.py says the consensus_edge flag defaults ON; feature_flags.py sets it False, and the live routes 503
claimUnderTest: server.py's comment at the router registration states the consensus_edge flag has defaulted ON since 2026-08-04.
observed: src/api/feature_flags.py:260 sets "consensus_edge": False with an ADR-023 rationale for the rollback, and every /api/consensus-edge/* route returns 503 {"error":"feature_disabled","flag":"consensus_edge"} on the running server. The code comment is the stale one — and it sits at the registration site a reader hits first.

reproduction.actual: comment says ON; default is False; routes 503

numericProof.formula: observed HTTP status against the documented flag default

userImpact: A maintainer reading server.py concludes the feature is live and will not look for the flag when the page renders nothing.

priorFinding.note: Found by diffing the comment against the registry and the live 503.

rootCause: ADR-023 flipped the flag back off without updating the comment written when it was turned on.
requiredRepair: Delete or correct the server.py comment; it duplicates state that feature_flags.py owns.

title: /api/health registers a duplicate OpenAPI operation ID, which pytest warns about on every run
observed: FastAPI emits 'UserWarning: Duplicate Operation ID get_health_api_health_get for function get_health' during schema generation; it appears in the pytest run output and in /openapi.json generation. The live schema carries 100 operations across 97 unique paths.

numericProof.formula: count of operations minus count of unique paths

userImpact: Generated clients and API docs get a colliding operation name; the warning also trains readers to ignore warnings in the test output.

priorFinding.note: Observed in this audit's own test run.

requiredRepair: Give the api_route registration an explicit distinct operation_id.

title: Four value fields coexist on every contract row and diverge by up to 35.6%, with _finalAdjusted still read by a legacy branch of the arbitrage finder
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Both engines now read the same internal value' — finder.py reads the canonical board via board_values_from_contract.
observed: Every row carries rankDerivedValue AND _finalAdjusted AND _composite AND _rawComposite AND (for offense) _offenseOnlyFinalAdjusted. Measured divergence of _finalAdjusted from the served rankDerivedValue: Carson Schwesinger +35.6%, Aidan Hutchinson +30.6%, Brock Bowers +6.8%, Travis Etienne -9.5%. finder.py's PRIMARY path does read the board — the _finalAdjusted reads at :498 sit in an explicit `else:` legacy branch taken only when no contract is supplied, and :1006 uses it deliberately on the composite scale to count unpriced assets. So the CLAUDE.md claim is upheld for the live path; what remains open is whether any caller can reach the legacy branch.

reproduction.expected: one value concept per row, or clearly-scoped variants
reproduction.actual: four coexisting fields; _finalAdjusted differs from the served value by up to 35.6%

userImpact: Any consumer that reaches the legacy branch prices IDP assets ~30% below the board the user sees.

priorFinding.note: The headline 'the finder arbitrages an invisible board' does NOT reproduce at HEAD — the primary path reads board values. Recorded as refuted for the live path; the residual risk is the ungated legacy branch.

whatWorks: finder.py's primary path reads board_values_from_contract, and the scale reasoning at :478-497 is documented and correct.
rootCause: The migration to the canonical board left the legacy composite path in place as a fallback rather than removing it.
requiredRepair: Establish whether any live caller passes contract=None; if not, delete the legacy branch rather than leaving two scales reachable.

title: Confidence reads High on two-source pick rows while fourteen-source player rows read Medium
claimUnderTest: Confidence communicates how much evidence stands behind a number.
observed: 2027 Early 1st (sourceCount 2) is labelled 'High — picks agree within 15%'. 2028 Late 1st (sourceCount 2) likewise. Travis Etienne (sourceCount 14) and George Kittle (sourceCount 14) are labelled 'Medium — multi-source, moderate spread'. The rule is agreement-based, which is defensible, but the rendered word inverts the evidence ordering: two sources agreeing outranks fourteen sources disagreeing slightly.

reproduction.expected: a two-source row cannot outrank a fourteen-source row on displayed confidence

numericProof.formula: compare displayed confidence bucket against surviving source count

userImpact: A user reads High confidence on a future pick whose value rests on two correlated pick markets and discounts a player value backed by fourteen sources.

priorFinding.note: The prior audit claims a 33.3% confidence misclassification rate; W03 is measuring that independently. This is a distinct, directly-observable presentation defect.

rootCause: Agreement and evidence-volume are collapsed into one displayed word.
requiredRepair: Show source count alongside the bucket, or floor the bucket by count so a two-source row cannot render High.
dependencies: W03 owns the full confidence-calibration measurement.

title: A current-year pick's provenance fields name two different sources
claimUnderTest: Every visible number can identify its source (audit brief section 6).
observed: On 2026 Pick 1.01: sourceRanks = {'idpTradeCalc': 12} while sourceOriginalRanks = {'dlfRookieSf': 1.0}. The two provenance stamps on the same row name different sources, and only idpTradeCalc appears in the committed CSVs for that asset. Separately, 2027 Early 1st reports sourceCount 2 with sourceOriginalRanks = {} (empty).

reproduction.expected: provenance stamps agree on which sources produced the row
reproduction.actual: sourceRanks names idpTradeCalc; sourceOriginalRanks names dlfRookieSf

numericProof.formula: set intersection of the two provenance maps

userImpact: Provenance cannot be trusted to answer 'where did this number come from' for pick rows, which is precisely where values are thinnest.

priorFinding.note: Observed directly in the pick traces.

rootCause: Pick tethering overwrites the value from the merged rookie pool while the original-rank stamp survives from the pre-tether row.
requiredRepair: Stamp the tethering source on tethered rows so both maps describe the same provenance.

title: Measured through the production topology the frontend is clean: 41/41 pages load, 38 render an h1, median DOM-ready 83 ms, and the only client errors are correct auth and flag responses
claimUnderTest: The site's pages render and are usable.
observed: Every one of the 41 Next pages returns 200 authenticated. 38 render an <h1>. Median DOM-ready (navMs) is 83 ms, max 695 ms. Of 55 console errors, the only non-artifact ones are: 401 on / (one unauthenticated call from the home page), 403 on /admin (correct — the audit's test user is deliberately not in the admin allowlist) and 503 on /consensus-edge (correct — the flag is off per ADR-023). All 149 failed requests resolve to two harmless causes: ERR_ABORTED from the probe navigating away mid-flight, and sleepercdn.com avatar images, which this container cannot reach. Three redirects are by design: /finder -> /rankings, /intel -> /league/insider-trading, /rankings/qb -> /rankings?pos=QB.

reproduction.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python <scratchpad>/probe_pages.py  # loads all 41 pages anon+auth with nginx-equivalent /api/* interception

numericProof.formula: count of pages returning 200 with a rendered h1

userImpact: None — this is a clean bill of health for the page layer, recorded because the audit's own first two measurements wrongly suggested otherwise.

priorFinding.note: Supersedes this audit's own invalid captures: page-probe-direct-next-INVALID.json (222 console errors) and page-probe-via-proxy-INVALID.json (dead shells). See evidence/INTEGRITY.md.

whatWorks: The page layer. Bundles are all under the build's own budget, and DOM-ready is under 100 ms at the median.

title: Three public league sub-pages render no heading and under 180 characters of text — franchise, rivalry and article-preview are effectively blank
claimUnderTest: Franchise pages, rivalry pages and article previews are working public surfaces.
observed: With real values substituted into the dynamic segments (owner=jasonleetucker, pair=jasonleetucker-vs-blaine, season=2025 week=1 matchup=1 mode=preview), all three return HTTP 200 but render NO <h1> and 143, 156 and 176 characters of body text respectively — anonymously and authenticated alike. For comparison /league/player/4046 renders 1,610 characters with an h1 of 'Patrick Mahomes', and /league/week/2025/1 renders 3,982 characters. The three are reachable, linked, and empty.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/league/franchise/jasonleetucker | wc -c  # then compare rendered innerText via the page probe
reproduction.expected: a franchise page renders franchise content
reproduction.actual: 200 with no h1 and 143 characters of text

userImpact: A visitor following a franchise or rivalry link from the league hub lands on a blank page with no explanation — the worst of the three states (content, honest empty state, blank).

priorFinding.note: Whether the cause is a missing data join or a wrong URL-parameter format is W19's to determine — the owner slug and pair format used here were inferred.

rootCause: Unconfirmed: either the dynamic-segment format differs from what the page expects, or the backing data (week-level roster ownership / head-to-head history) is absent and the page renders nothing rather than saying so.
requiredRepair: Render an explicit empty state naming what is missing; if the segment format is the issue, make the page say so rather than returning 200 with nothing.
dependencies: W19 owns the public-league data-completeness question.
